stories.title: Global conference addresses mental health stigma
stories.summary: The 11th Together Against Stigma Conference opened on 12 November at AIIMS New Delhi. Organised by The George Institute, UNICEF India, and psychiatric associations, the three-day event gathers experts to discuss practical actions for reducing stigma and improving care. The conference concludes on 14 November 2026.

stories.title: Barboursville School to reopen as residential facility
stories.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey announced that the former Barboursville School will reopen next year as a residential treatment facility for children. The state has signed a five-year lease with Youth Health Associates to operate the site. The facility plans to begin accepting children in early 2027.

stories.title: Study examines youth mental health disclosures online
stories.summary: Researchers analysed 957 posts and 763 comments on Reddit and TikTok to investigate how young people disclose mental health challenges. Published in Discover Mental Health, the study examined the motivations behind these disclosures and how other users respond. The full piece is available for subscribers.

stories.title: Ole Miss expands mental health support for athletes
stories.summary: The University of Mississippi has built programs for student-athletes, including licensed counselors and media training. Shannon Singletary, who leads sports performance, stated the goal is to prevent anxiety and depression rather than just treating it. The university aims to help athletes excel in sport and life.

stories.title: University of Denver offers low-cost veteran care
stories.summary: A study found nearly half of post 9/11 veterans suffer from depression, anxiety, or PTSD, highlighting an unmet need for care. The University of Denver Sturm Center provides low-cost services, with faculty advocating for evidence-based, community-focused mental health support to address these ongoing service member needs.

stories.title: Maxwell professor researches mindfulness in Brazil
stories.summary: Dessa Bergen-Cico, a professor at the Maxwell School, is spending three weeks in São Paulo as a Fulbright Specialist. She is teaching graduate courses and researching how mindfulness practices, such as meditation and breathing exercises, can support community well-being in collaboration with the University of São Paulo.

stories.title: Study explores physiological shifts during meditation
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of North Texas evaluated how meditation affects human physiological processes. The study, published in Frontiers in Network Physiology, suggests that practice leads to a temporary reduction in scaling exponents, followed by an elevated level of complexity across brain and heart dynamics after meditation ends.

stories.title: Loyola program brings trauma-responsive care to jail
stories.summary: Dr. Marquitta Dorsey of Loyola University Chicago co-created EMPOWER, a program for incarcerated women at Cook County Jail. The initiative uses trauma-responsive practices, including guided breathing and singing bowls, to create a space for healing within the facility. The program operates during weekly morning sessions.

stories.title: BuDhaGirl founder urges focus on intentional rituals
stories.summary: Jessica Jesse, CEO of BuDhaGirl, challenged wellness leaders at the Global Wellness Summit to look beyond performance metrics. She advocated for a philosophy of mindful glamour, urging the industry to measure success by the everyday rituals people continue to practice after leaving a wellness destination.

stories.title: Potadóir opens in Ennis as mindful craft space
stories.summary: Potadóir, a new studio in Ennis, combines pottery workshops with a yoga space. Founded by Kevin Keane and Dzana, the hub offers ceramics inspired by The Burren landscape alongside holistic wellness classes. The business was established following Keane's recovery from a car crash in 2022.

stories.title: Muse users' brain data used to train AI
stories.summary: Interaxon, maker of the Muse headband, used 50,000 hours of customer brainwave recordings to train a brain foundation model without explicit user consent, according to Science magazine. The company acknowledges that users should have been informed. The data may help identify patterns associated with neurological events.

stories.title: Swedish grain study finds health and environment metrics diverge
stories.summary: A study in Frontiers in Nutrition examined the relationship between health benefits and environmental impacts for 297 grain products in Sweden. Researchers found that high nutritional density does not guarantee low environmental footprints. Health impacts and ecological sustainability do not necessarily align in the grain aisle.

stories.title: Irregular sleep schedules linked to mental health
stories.summary: A study of 20,000 participants found that inconsistent bedtimes and wake times are linked to higher symptoms of depression, anxiety, and loneliness. The correlation persisted regardless of total sleep duration. Researchers suggest that sleep regularity may be as important as the total number of hours spent in bed.

stories.title: Sleep expert recommends 17 hours awake
stories.summary: Lee Jun-yong suggests avoiding bed until at least 17 hours have passed since waking. The expert links sleep deprivation to mental health issues and recommends exercise and warm showers to improve rest quality. The advice prioritizes wakefulness duration as a primary factor for better sleep hygiene.

stories.title: Sleep apnea symptoms persist despite time in bed
stories.summary: A case study highlights how sleep apnea can cause chronic fatigue and headaches, even when patients spend significant time in bed. The condition involves breathing interruptions that prevent restorative rest. Patients often mistake these symptoms for other health issues while struggling to remain alert during daily activities.

stories.title: Group insomnia therapy shows promise in community health
stories.summary: A service evaluation in London found that a six-week group program of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia led to clinically meaningful reductions in sleep disturbance. Therapeutic gains persisted for three months among participants. The evaluation also noted significant systemic friction within the community mental health services involved.

stories.title: Pink noise shows potential for Alzheimer’s memory loss
stories.summary: A small study of 37 people with early-stage Alzheimer’s suggests that brief bursts of pink noise during sleep may provide a memory boost. Researchers are investigating whether the low-pitched hiss helps clear waste products from the brain. Further study is required to confirm the therapeutic benefits.

stories.title: Hypnic jerks linked to anxiety and poor sleep
stories.summary: A study of 194 adults found that frequent hypnic jerks, or sleep starts, are associated with poorer sleep quality and higher anxiety levels. Participants reported more episodes during periods of emotional stress. The sudden muscle twitches can be strong enough to jolt a person fully awake.

stories.title: Irregular sleep linked to worse anxiety and depression

stories.title: Poor sleep quality linked to lower physical fitness
stories.summary: A school-based investigation of 5,018 Chinese adolescents found a modest association between poor sleep quality and lower physical fitness. The study, published in Frontiers in Pediatrics, addressed a gap in understanding how sleep affects adolescent health. Researchers used the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index to measure sleep patterns.

stories.summary: People who keep irregular sleep-wake schedules may experience more severe symptoms of depression, anxiety, and loneliness, according to a large study led by researchers at the University of California, San Francisco and the University of California, San Diego. Published in Scientific Reports, the investigation shifted

stories.summary: Reallocating daily time from nocturnal sleep, sedentary behavior, or moderate-to-vigorous physical activity toward walking is associated with lower odds of calcaneal quantitative ultrasound-defined osteoporosis among rural adults, according to a cross-sectional study. Prior research had largely evaluated the independent effects of physical activity, sleep, and

stories.summary: In her 70s, Oprah continues to prioritise movement, often posting online about the workouts and exercises she’s using to future-proof her body. The multi-hyphenate has been candid about her use of GLP-1s to and the important role exercise can play in maintaining muscle, bone and

stories.title: Home exercises for walking speed
stories.summary: A report suggests specific home exercises may restore walking speed faster than treadmills for those over 70. The piece, published by Eat This Not That, remains behind a paywall for those who do not enable cookies and JavaScript to continue reading the full list of recommendations.

stories.title: Mel B shares wellness routine at 51
stories.summary: Spice Girls star Mel B says she has adapted her fitness routine to manage menopause symptoms. Her current regimen includes infrared sunshowers, Himalayan salt saunas, ice baths and collagen coffee. The singer says she uses these activities to support her mental and physical wellbeing.

stories.title: Trainers on exercise after 65
stories.summary: A report from Eat This Not That claims trainers agree walking is insufficient for maintaining leg strength after 65. The article suggests five specific exercises to address this, though the full details remain inaccessible to readers who do not enable cookies and JavaScript on the site.

stories.title: High-intensity sports and bone formation
stories.summary: A review of 24 studies suggests vigorous sports like football and handball may stimulate bone formation more effectively than walking or resistance training. Researchers at Semmelweis University analyzed blood markers in 1,238 adults. The study focuses on bone metabolism rather than mineral density.

stories.title: Liz Earle on strength training
stories.summary: Wellness entrepreneur Liz Earle says she maintains her fitness at 63 through short, consistent strength training sessions. She claims that workouts of up to 20 minutes can make a massive difference in building muscle. The routine is intended to support independence and longevity in later life.

stories.title: Podiatrist-approved foot exercises
stories.summary: London podiatrist Steven Thomas prescribes lower-limb resistance training to help walkers and runners protect their joints and tendons. The exercises aim to mitigate the wear and tear associated with increased mileage. The routine is designed to improve performance and lighten the load on the feet.

stories.title: Sports linked to bone formation markers
stories.summary: Researchers at Semmelweis University found that sports involving sharp turns and acceleration may increase bone formation markers by up to 46 percent. The study, published in Sports Medicine to Open, assessed blood biomarkers in 1,238 adults. The findings suggest intensity matters for skeletal health.

stories.title: New mindful eating scales for families
stories.summary: Researchers have developed the Mindful Eating Behaviour Scale for Children and Parents to address methodological gaps in paediatric research. The tools measure sustained attention to sensory elements during meals and non-judgmental awareness of internal states. The project aims to improve the precision of dietary pattern studies.

stories.title: Gut virome role in human health
stories.summary: A review in the Virology Journal examines the human gut virome, describing it as a significant regulator of health and disease prevention. The study suggests shifting research focus from bacterial communities to the viral fraction of the microbiome. The virome remains an under-studied component of gastrointestinal health.

stories.title: Study promotes Eastern Healthy diet
stories.summary: Researchers from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention suggest adopting traditional dietary patterns from China's southeastern coastal regions to reduce health risks. The study notes that shifts toward meat and dairy consumption have coincided with rising obesity and cardiovascular disease rates across the country.

stories.title: Nutrition services in professional rugby
stories.summary: A study of Australian professional rugby union suggests that while nutrition is considered foundational, its practical impact is limited by organizational undervaluation. Research indicates that staffing remains largely part-time and responsibilities are often blurred. Nutrition services currently struggle to function as intended in high-performance environments.

stories.title: Nutrition program outcomes in Nepal
stories.summary: A study published in Maternal & Child Nutrition reports that the Suaahara program improved nutrition in target districts in Nepal. Researchers led by Edward Frongillo found key health improvements compared to areas without the program. Undernutrition remains a prevalent public health challenge in the region.

stories.title: Mediterranean diet and pancreatic fat
stories.summary: An 18-month study suggests a plant-rich Mediterranean diet may reduce fat stored inside the pancreas by 14 percent. Researchers believe this could assist with blood-sugar control. The findings come with qualifications, as the study specifically highlights the role of plant compounds known as polyphenols.

stories.title: Gut-brain axis and health products
stories.summary: The gut-brain axis is a two-way communication network linking the microbiome to the brain via neural and hormonal pathways. Brands are increasingly looking to this science to develop products for stress, sleep and mood. Shoppers now want evidence of how these products function biologically.

stories.title: Factors affecting blood sugar levels
stories.summary: Diabetologist Dr. Suman Banerjee explains that daily habits like skipping meals or changing medication routines can influence blood sugar regulation. Understanding these fluctuations is presented as a key component of managing overall health. The advice is intended to help patients recognize when changes require attention.

stories.title: Nutritionist on kitchen swaps
stories.summary: Nutritionist Aditi Prasad Apte offers guidance on kitchen swaps for oil, rice and snacks to support weight loss and blood sugar management. The advice is part of a series intended to bridge the gap between social media fads and evidence-based clinical guidance for daily routines.

stories.title: Animal models and biological aging
stories.summary: Researchers writing in Nature Aging suggest that animal models may help identify the biological pathways connecting social adversity to accelerated aging. While human studies show links between low social status and chronic illness, the specific causal mechanisms remain difficult to isolate in observational research.

stories.title: Environmental resilience and aging
stories.summary: A review in Nature Aging examines why aging trajectories differ among populations exposed to similar environmental risks like pollution or extreme temperatures. The authors propose that environmental health resilience factors, such as built and social environments, may act as protective modifiers to flatten the exposure response curve.

stories.title: Dr Shriram Nene on healthy ageing
stories.summary: Dr Shriram Nene suggests that longevity relies on nutrition, movement, sleep, stress management, and purpose. He advises scepticism toward anti-ageing supplements, IV drips, and wellness fads, favouring consistent daily habits instead. The secret to living longer may be simple, provided one is actually doing it.

stories.title: Russian longevity research uses 7,000 monkeys
stories.summary: Mikhail Kovalchuk, an informal scientific advisor to Vladimir Putin, is leading a study on the ageing process using 7,000 primates. The research focuses on elderly monkeys between 20 and 30 years old. The project aims to expand human potential through primate observation.

stories.title: Shared meals linked to improved blood glucose
stories.summary: A study of 108 people suggests that eating with loved ones can improve healthspan by lowering blood glucose levels. Researchers examined how social proximity influences physiological responses during meals. Sharing a Thanksgiving dinner may now be classified as a medical intervention.

stories.title: Probiotic strain linked to mood and sleep improvements
stories.summary: A clinical trial found that a specific probiotic strain improved mood, sleep, and digestion in older adults after eight weeks. The study highlights the connection between the gut microbiome and mental health. Bacteria are increasingly being asked to manage human emotions.

stories.title: Frontiers retracts 2022 fisetin study
stories.summary: Frontiers in Pharmacology has retracted a 2022 study on fisetin and cellular damage due to image integrity concerns. The journal deemed the data and conclusions unreliable following an investigation into the published figures. The science has been removed from the record.

stories.title: Horse-assisted therapy reduces stress in autistic children
stories.summary: Research from Colorado State University indicates that occupational therapy involving horses lowers the physiological stress response in autistic children. While the interaction is often described as magic, the study provides empirical data to explain the effect. The horses remain indifferent to the data.

stories.title: Cheff Therapeutic Riding Center expands
stories.summary: The Cheff Therapeutic Riding Center has opened the Suzanne U.D. Parish Therapy Arena to increase capacity for riding therapy. The facility provides private spaces for individuals with mental health issues to work with specialists and horses. The horses are now working in a larger arena.

stories.title: Trump administration to fund psychedelics research
stories.summary: The Trump administration plans to invest millions into research regarding the use of psychedelics for mental health treatment. The Washington Post reports the funding initiative aims to explore new therapeutic applications. The administration is betting on substances previously classified as illicit.

stories.title: Lavender aromatherapy tested for sleep disorder
stories.summary: A Japanese study found that bedside lavender aromatherapy was associated with symptom relief in seven out of nine patients with treatment-resistant REM sleep behavior disorder. The condition involves physically enacting dreams. The scent of lavender is being tested against violent sleep.

stories.title: ARPA-H invests in ibogaine for PTSD
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services will provide up to $4.9 million over five years to develop ibogaine as a treatment for PTSD. The agency plans to evaluate the drug for substance use disorders as well. The government is betting on a psychedelic future.

stories.title: Yoga protocol linked to brain connectivity
stories.summary: A 45-day study of the government-standardised Common Yoga Protocol found improvements in memory, sleep, and brain connectivity in healthy adults. Researchers used fMRI scans to observe changes in how brain regions communicate. The study is the first randomised trial to neuroimage this specific protocol.

stories.title: Psychedelic drug design in mental health
stories.summary: Psychedelic-assisted therapy aims to disrupt established patterns of brain activity by targeting serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. Research suggests this creates a temporary window where psychological patterns are more open to change. The treatment involves short, intense experiences rather than long-term medication.

stories.title: Overseas patients visit Belagavi for Ayurveda
stories.summary: Patients from Germany, Bulgaria, and Australia recently travelled to Belagavi for Ayurvedic consultations and Panchakarma therapies. The hospital staff provided personalized diet and lifestyle guidance alongside traditional treatments. The patients expressed satisfaction with the care they received.

stories.title: Phage therapy potential in antimicrobial resistance
stories.summary: Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy Koganti suggests that phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to eliminate bacteria, could help combat antimicrobial resistance. The research was presented at an international symposium. The approach relies on using viruses to kill bacteria.

stories.title: Beijing doctor uses needle therapy for allergies
stories.summary: A Beijing-based doctor is using a family-practiced needling therapy derived from acupuncture to treat autumn allergic rhinitis. The clinic aims to provide an affordable alternative to standard allergy treatments. The weeds continue to release pollen regardless of the needles.
